title: Complete Classification of Positive-Slope Relative-Bound Equiangular Line Families, Exact Fixed-Angle Thresholds, Consecutive-Dimension Extensions, and Unconditional Leech d_4(C) = 204
abstract: Djaljapayan, Liao, and Yu (arXiv:2611.34855v1) determined N(18) = 57, N(19) = 72, and N(20) = 90, computed the first three generalized Hamming weights (100, 150, 186) of the Co_3-invariant Leech [276, 23, 100] binary evaluation code C, and combined repeated-Seidel-block constructions with the Bukh-Cox coherence bound (Section 5) to establish exact fixed-angle values N_{1/q}(d) = d + k on linearly growing intervals for k = 7 (all odd q >= 319) and k = 23 (all odd q >= 5599), together with a single-dimension quadratic-irrational family from symmetric conference matrices (Theorem 5.2) and two isolated values at cosine 1/7 (Proposition 5.3). We systematically complete and sharpen every component of that program. First (Theorem 1), we prove an exact linear-in-a classification showing that among all nontrivial relative-bound two-eigenvalue equiangular seeds (k, M, a) (2 <= k <= a^2 - 2, M <= k(k+1)/2), positive Bukh-Cox slope L_k > M/b holds if and only if k in {3, 5, 6, 7} for a = 3 and exclusively k in {a^2 - 3, a^2 - 2} for every odd a >= 5; on k = a^2 - 3, L_{a^2-3} = (a^2-2)(a+1)/((a-1)(a+2)) and its slope a(a+1)/((a-1)(a+2)(a^2+a-3)) are exact rational. Second (Theorem 2), via the exact alternating-character range lambda_alt(A) in {-3, -2, -1, 0, 1} (sharpening Q - 2r to Q - 6), r <= b - 1, and explicit {+-1}^M seed eigenvectors S v = -a v enabling odd-t repetitions with constant Schur ratio rho = k/a, we obtain four new infinite families -- Tetrahedron k = 3 (q >= 7), Petersen k = 5 (q >= 155; q >= 11 for q = 3 mod 4), Clebsch k = 6 (q >= 161; q >= 89 for q = 1 mod 4), and Higman-Sims k = 22 (q >= 8643) -- while sharpening both published thresholds (k = 7: 319 -> 245, and 125 for q = 1 mod 4; k = 23: 5599 -> 5267) and proving exact zero-gap adjacent contact d_+^(6) + 1 = d_-^(7) (10 | Q) and d_+^(22) + 1 = d_-^(23) (112 | Q). Third (Theorem 3), we upgrade Theorem 5.2 to consecutive intervals of length (sqrt(m^2 + 2m) - m)t + O(1) for every even t >= 2, generalize Proposition 5.3 to infinite s in {2, 3} relative-bound block windows for all odd q >= 5 (catching exact Pell jumps at (15, 25) and (35, 49)), and prove an exact s >= 4 impossibility barrier. Fourth (Theorem 4, added in Version 2), we prove unconditionally -- independently of the 23-Niemeier classification of N(19) = 72 -- that the fourth generalized Hamming weight of the Leech code is d_4(C) = 204, eliminating all 420 isomorphic PG(3, 2) constraint-satisfaction survivors at support 203 via the universal fourth-moment integer inequality t^4 - 4t^2 >= -3 * 1_{t odd}, and explicitly construct the four-normal section V_{19} = ker(y_a, y_{O_1}, y_b, y_{O_2}) (with O_1 cap O_2 = {a, b}) of 72 = N(19) axes of exact rank 19, extending the optimal nested Leech chain across all five dimensions 23 -> 19 (276 -> 176 -> 126 -> 90 -> 72) before dropping to 56 < 57 = N(18) in R^{18}. All 24 core algebraic theorems are formally verified in constructive Lean 4.36.0 (0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice, 0 custom axioms) and backed by 20 AST-audited zero-float SHA-256 certificates and 64 adversarial tests.
